         1                  SENATOR KLEIN:    Madam President,

         7                  SENATOR LARKIN:    Thank you very

         8       much, Madam President.

         9                  You know, the month of May has been

        10       dedicated as Military Appreciation Month.  And

        11       I don't think there's a better time of the

        12       year to take a good look at what the military

        13       means.

        14                  First of all, it's been designated

        15       by Congress.  At least they all agreed -- it

        16       was unanimous in both houses on both sides of

        17       the aisle -- to make May Military Appreciation

        18       Month.

        19                  But if you look at this, this is an

        20       opportunity for us, a golden opportunity for

        21       us to get our young people involved so that

        22       they will know what the military is all about.

        23       It isn't about watching TV on Sunday night or

        24       Tuesday night and seeing caskets come home,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3914



         1       it's about what they stand for, what they mean

         2       to us as a country.

         3                  You know, if you look at May, it's

         4       VE Day in Europe.  If you look at it, it's

         5       Armed Forces Day, it's Loyalty Day, it's the

         6       National Day of Prayer, and finally, it's

         7       Memorial Day.  The month honors all of our

         8       brothers and sisters who served in the armed

         9       forces and many who didn't come home.

        10                  As of the first of this month,

        11       there was a recorded 1.8 million Americans

        12       have received the Purple Heart, either

        13       directly or posthumously, for being wounded or

        14       killed in combat.  There are 590 as of the

        15       first of May still alive who have received

        16       this award.

        17                  This is Military Appreciation

        18       Month.  And I think that everybody here in

        19       this chamber, regardless of what you think

        20       about war, what you think about those of us

        21       who served in one, two, or three -- but what

        22       those men and women that served with us did,

        23       they did it for us, for us, for our future,

        24       for our future generations.



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         1                  And I think we have a due

         2       responsibility to put out the word that this

         3       is Military Appreciation Month and to

         4       encourage all of our constituents to stand up

         5       and proudly say "Thank you for your service to

         6       our country."
